LESSON: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: FICTION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: why reading fiction materials is important. 1. Which story books or plays have you read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. appreciate the importance of reading fiction for exposure

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction

Teach
• Focus skill: appreciate the importance of reading fiction for exposure.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. why reading fiction materials is important. 1. Which story books or plays have you read?
2. What makes a book interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
